research_scope: Source-free complete mathematical dependency scans of 12 existing independent formulations; reference linking and unassigned occurrences only; no new terms, citations or external source browsing.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire Krull-topology formulation and distinguished field Galois structure, topological continuity, discrete codomain and profiniteness; recorded the initial-topology and evaluation-map constructions without external research.

references.matching_note: The definition explicitly assumes E/F is Galois; match the existing Galois field-extension meaning.
The automorphisms fixing F form the relative Galois group, not a generic group alone.

references.phrase: weakest topology making every evaluation map continuous
references.matching_note: Uses open-set topology on the Galois group; the weakest/initial construction is separately unassigned.
Evaluation maps into E with its discrete topology are continuous under the stated source topology.
The codomain E is equipped with its full-power-set topology; E nonempty as a field.
The text explicitly asserts that the resulting topological Galois group is profinite.

references.phrase: weakest topology making every evaluation map continuous
references.context: Topology: initial topology generated on Gal(E/F) by evaluation maps into discrete E
references.reason: The existing topological-space and continuity definitions do not separately name the initial-topology construction; record it for global classification without outside research.

references.context: Galois theory: evaluation at a fixed field element a on automorphisms of E/F
references.reason: The point-evaluation construction has not been shown to have a stand-alone contextual meaning; save the occurrence, not a distinct new term.

items.review_rationale: Read the complete Noetherian constructible-subset formulation and checked the available Noetherian topology, subset and topological-space meanings. Finite union/intersection needs no source investigation.

references.matching_note: Directly names the existing Noetherian-space context.
The ordinary non-strict inclusion relation C⊆X is supported by the generic subset definition.
Openness is relative to the topology on X, not the patch topology of the space of spectra.
Closed sets here are complements of open sets in the given topological space.

references.disposition: This is ordinary finite set union and intersection, used directly with open and closed subsets; a separate new mathematical contextual meaning is not presumed.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the short associate-elements definition in an integral domain, identified a ring unit as the inverse witness, and treated multiplication as ambient ring structure without creating a missing definition.

references.matching_note: Integral domain has the same nonzero commutative unital ring convention as this associate relation.
An invertible multiplicative ring element is a unit; distinguish the unity element itself.

references.disposition: The product and equality are the inherited ring multiplication and equality on elements, not a second independent named construction.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the entire Dedekind-domain factorization characterization and distinguished existing domain/ideals/prime ideals from the still-unclassified operation of multiplying ideals; no source lookup was performed.

references.matching_note: The definition restricts to nonzero commutative unital integral domains.
A commutative-ring ideal is a two-sided ring ideal; nonzero is a property, not another ideal type.
Proper prime ideals are in the same unital commutative domain; explicitly matches ring primes.

references.phrase: finite product of nonzero prime ideals
references.context: Commutative algebra: multiplication of ring ideals and finite products of ideals in a commutative unital integral domain
references.reason: Neither general ideal nor prime-ideal axioms themselves define multiplication of ideals; record this construction without source research.

references.phrase: unique up to permuting the factors
references.disposition: Equality of finite factorizations modulo reordering factors is the ordinary symmetric equivalence for a finite list, and does not itself require a new named definition in this scan.

items.review_rationale: Read the irreducibility condition with its domain, nonzero condition, unit and factorization clauses; linked unit and integral domain and treated ordinary multiplication as ambient.

references.matching_note: Ambient integral domain has the established commutative-unital convention.
Nonunit and unit factor are uses of exactly the ring-unit meaning.

references.disposition: A two-element factorization is equality under the ring's own multiplication; record as a basic operation rather than asserting a new notion.
Nonzero denotes inequality with the additive identity of the ambient ring and needs no separate named meaning here.

items.review_rationale: Checked all finite-factorization and uniqueness clauses of the UFD characterization; linked the specific irreducible, unit, associate and domain meanings without researching additional terms.

references.matching_note: The factorization takes place in a nonzero commutative unital integral domain.
Nonunit is the negation of membership among the ring's invertible elements.
Irreducible factors refer to the already indexed context-specific irreducible-element definition.
Equality of factors up to multiplication by invertible elements is the associate-elements relation.

references.disposition: Reordering a finite product is a standard permutation of a finite factor list in a commutative multiplication, not an additional unexplained contextual meaning.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the ordinal-representative definition of cardinality, linked the existing ordinal and well-order notions, and preserved separate equipotence and bijection occurrences for global consolidation.

references.matching_note: The least ordinal representative is an ordinal in the indexed set-theoretic sense.
The meaning of least ordinal uses the usual well-ordering of ordinals, rather than arbitrary cardinal arithmetic.

references.context: Set theory: equinumerosity of two sets established by existence of a bijection
references.reason: The occurrence should be globally compared with bijections/equipotence elsewhere before any new definition is researched.

references.context: Set theory: bijective map between two sets, one of which is A
references.reason: This may be the construction underlying equipotence, but the first pass should not yet merge their contextual meaning identities.

references.disposition: A is an arbitrary set, treated as the ambient foundational object rather than presuming another newly discovered mathematical term.

items.review_rationale: Examined the complete spectrum clopen-subset characterization, linked the existing prime spectrum/topology/prime ideals and preserved idempotent, distinguished open and commutative unital ring occurrences.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative ring with multiplicative identity
references.reason: Shares the already recorded missing commutative-unital ring context; do not source-research it before global occurrence consolidation.

Clopen is openness and closedness in the ambient spectrum topology; the topological-space axioms supply these predicates.
Points p of the prime spectrum correspond to prime ideals in the commutative unital ring.

references.reason: Idempotency is an independent named algebraic property, not the same as an ideal or the unit of a ring.

references.reason: D(e) is described explicitly by primes not containing e, but a separate principal distinguished open construction may be needed; defer classification.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the full categorical compactness comparison, distinguished filtered indexing and colimit meanings from arbitrary category/Hom/canonical map/bijection occurrences, without imposing unsupported smallness.

references.reason: Existing small-category meaning adds size restrictions that do not follow from this arbitrary category C; do not make an invalid confident link.

The defining comparison uses the filtered colimit of M_i when it exists.
The source of the comparison is a colimit of Hom sets, interpreted as a diagram of sets; don't confuse this with a module colimit.

references.context: Category theory: set or class of morphisms between two objects in a category C
references.reason: The Hom construction and potential size issue warrant later classification; no unverified blanket smallness assumption.

references.context: Set theory and category theory: bijective map of Hom sets in the categorical compactness test

items.review_rationale: Read both 2-morphism invertibility and hom-groupoid clauses in the strict (2,1)-category definition, linking existing 2-category/groupoid concepts while deferring the composition-operation classification.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed G-unramified-at-a-prime as a property of an unital commutative ring map after localization, linking the prime ideal, localization and G-unramified ring-map meaning in their precise contexts.

S_g localizes S at the multiplicative powers of g, which is the existing ring-localization construction.
G-unramified is the matching property of the localized ring map.

references.disposition: The g∉q condition is ordinary set non-membership and needs no new named notion.

items.review_rationale: Read the complete Stacks-style G-unramified ring-map condition, distinguished ring finite presentation from module finite presentation and linked Kähler differentials and the appropriate ring homomorphism.

references.matching_note: The Stacks convention for commutative rings uses unital ring homomorphisms; the nonunital alternative is not silently substituted.
The source requires finite presentation of the ring map R→S, not the separate finite presentation of a module.
Kähler differentials are the existing independently indexed module attached to S/R.

references.disposition: Equality with the zero module is the ordinary zero-object condition in an S-module, not by itself an additional named definition in this source-free scan.
